english: to make a long story short
also: to cut a long story short

terms.gloss: to cut a long story short, to be brief
terms.grammar: purpose clause, used parenthetically; the neuter longum
evidence: Hor. S. 1.3.137: nē longum faciam (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Cat. 3.10: ac, nē longum sit, Quirītēs, tabellās prōferrī jussimus (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: not to go on too long
terms.comment: Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections in this form; Traupman is the only evidence.
Traupman’s second form; the classical phrase has the neuter, nē longum faciam, with no noun understood.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 108.
